The petitioners filed these petitions U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09-12-2018.
2. The petition averments in brief are as under:

On 09-12-2018 at about 3.40 p.m., the petitioner in both the cases were travelling in a Auto Rickshaw bearing No. AP.03.U.8907 to attend Swamy Ayyappa Bajana at Gunsisettipalli village of Kuppam taluk, Chittoor district,
Andhra Pradesh, the driver of the auto was proceeding in his extreme left side and when he reached near Heritage Milk dairy on NH-42, near Shanthipuram in between V Kote and Kuppam road, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing No.

Due to the impact, both petitioners sustained grievous injuries.

The petitioner in MVC No. 2677/2019 was shifted to PES Medical College hospital, Kuppam wherein first aid treatment was given and shifted to Victoria hospital,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and further shifted to Sparsh hospital and for further treatment he was shifted to Maruthi Speciality hospital, Andhra Pradesh, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.
At the time of accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 30 years, doing mason work and earning Rs.700/- to 800/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner is not able to continue with his work, suffering from permanent disability and lost his  SCCH-17 5 MVC No. 2677 & 2678 /2019 earning capacity.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.23,00,000/-.

The petitioner in MVC 2678/2019 was shifted to PES Medical College hospital, Kuppam wherein he took V. Ramamurthy vs Nallannagari Gopalappa on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10461028/

At the time of accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 22 years and working as a cleaner in a bus and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m. with bata of Rs.100/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner is not able to continue with his work, suffering from permanent disability and lost his earning capacity.

The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

It is further submitted that, the offending Tata Ace Goods Vehicle bearing No. AP.03.TE.4842 was insured with the 2nd respondent and the policy was valid at the time of accident.

There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioners in the absence of  SCCH-17 16 MVC No. 2677 & 2678 /2019 rebuttal evidence.

AP.03.TE.4842 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.

(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.
But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.

In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss  SCCH-17 26 MVC No. 2677 & 2678 /2019 of earning capacity due to disability.

This makes it clear that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent V. Ramamurthy vs Nallannagari Gopalappa on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10461028/

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

 ORDER
The petitions filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act are hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner in MVC No.2677/2019 is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,25,200/-(Rupees Four lakhs twenty five thousand two hundred only).
The petitioner is entitled for the interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding on the amount awarded under future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.

The petitioners filed these petitions U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09-12-2018.
Due to the impact, both petitioners sustained grievous injuries.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner is not able to continue with his work, suffering from permanent disability and lost his  SCCH-17 5 MVC No. 2677 & 2678 /2019 earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the  SCCH-17 15 MVC No. 2677 & 2678 /2019 standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioners in the absence of  SCCH-17 16 MVC No. 2677 & 2678 /2019 rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioners sustained injuries in the accident took place on 09-12-2018 which is caused by the driver of the Tata Ace Goods Vehicles bearing No.
AP.03.TE.4842 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e.,
